prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

Scottish National Party (SNP) Manifesto 2017—Summary (≤500 words)

Core message
- Vote SNP to oppose Conservative austerity, protect public services and family incomes, secure Scotland’s voice in Brexit, keep Single Market access, and uphold Scotland’s right to choose its future (potential independence referendum).

Record and values
- SNP MPs have opposed austerity, secured fairer devolution finance, challenged welfare cuts (including the “Rape Clause”), backed WASPI women, advanced action on domestic violence (Istanbul Convention), resisted Trident renewal, opposed Syria bombing, fought punitive benefit sanctions, exposed tax evasion via Scottish Limited Partnerships, and defended fair immigration cases.
- In Scotland: record NHS investment and staffing; free prescriptions; expanded free childcare; free university tuition; lower council tax; free personal care; highest UK housebuilding rate; higher youth employment; more police and lower crime; Bedroom Tax mitigated.

Key pledges
- End austerity with a fiscal plan balancing the current budget by 2021/22, reducing debt/GDP, releasing ~£120bn UK-wide for services and investment.
- Fair tax: UK-wide 50p top rate; oppose VAT/NI rises; reverse married couple’s allowance and bank levy cuts; tax bankers’ bonuses; no further corporation tax cuts.
- NHS: increase UK health spending; oppose privatisation; pass consequentials to Scotland; strengthen mental health; protect EU staff; seek EMA/EHIC continuity.
- Education: 30 hours free childcare for 3–4-year-olds and eligible 2s; invest to close the attainment gap; no grammar schools; maintain free tuition; restore post-study work visa; protect EU research/ERASMUS.
- Welfare and equality: scrap benefit freeze; abolish two-child cap and “Rape Clause”; uprate benefits by at least CPI; halt sanctions regime; fix Universal Credit; abolish Bedroom Tax UK-wide; protect disabled people’s incomes; restore bereavement support; commence socio-economic duty; end DWP premium-rate lines; restore housing support for 18–21s.
- Pensions: protect Triple Lock; support WASPI; oppose raising state pension age beyond 66; create Independent Savings & Pension Commission; extend auto-enrolment.
- Jobs, productivity, and business: double Employment Allowance; extend Annual Investment Allowance to £1m; strong industrial strategy; tackle late payments; simplify tax for SMEs; phase digital tax reporting; invest in infrastructure (roads, rail, homes, broadband to 100% by 2021).
- Oil & gas: targeted incentives, exploration support, late-life asset tax reform, decommissioning infrastructure, diversification; make industry a Brexit priority.
- Economy and trade: keep Single Market membership to protect jobs, wages and sectors (food & drink, universities); secure GIs; protect EU citizens’ rights; tailor immigration to Scotland; oppose skills charge.
- Rural and fisheries: return EU farm/fish powers and funding to Scotland; pay Scotland’s £190m CAP “convergence uplift”; protect processing workforce; improve broadband/mobile; end unfair delivery charges.
- Democracy: proportional representation for Commons; votes at 16 and for resident EU citizens; abolish House of Lords; strengthen Electoral Commission; fair campaign rules.
- Defence and foreign policy: scrap Trident and reinvest in services; invest in conventional defence and Scottish bases/shipbuilding; maintain Europol cooperation; curb problematic arms sales; support UN-led peace and human rights.
- Environment: expand low-cost renewables (on/offshore wind, tidal, wave), storage and interconnectors; lead on CCS; reform grid transmission charges; oppose Hinkley C; tough climate targets; oppose fox-hunting; maintain moratoria on fracking/UCG.
- International development and refugees: maintain 0.7% aid, climate justice focus, ethical trade; reopen Dubs scheme; fair, humane asylum with detention limits and integration strategy.

Scotland’s choice
- Seek a place at Brexit talks and Single Market inclusion. If SNP wins a majority of Scottish seats, it reinforces Holyrood’s mandate to determine timing of an independence referendum once Brexit terms are known.
